name: digest
title: Create hash function digests for arbitrary R objects or files

origin.description: Apply a hash to an R object or a file. By default the object is serialized first, and the 14-byte serialization header is skipped so the digest does not depend on the R version.
origin.usage: digest(object, algo = c("md5", "sha1", "crc32", "sha256", "sha512", "xxhash32", "xxhash64", "murmur32", "spookyhash", "blake3", "crc32c", "xxh3_64", "xxh3_128"), serialize = TRUE, file = FALSE, length = Inf, skip = "auto", ascii = FALSE, raw = FALSE, seed = 0, errormode = c("stop", "warn", "silent"), serializeVersion = .getSerializeVersion())

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: An R object. Passed to serialize unless serialize is FALSE, in which case it must be a character string or a raw vector.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: Hash algorithm. A unique prefix is accepted. md5 is the default.

arguments.name: serialize
arguments.text: If TRUE, hash the version-2 serialization of the object.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: If TRUE, object is a file path. A character file with object missing is treated the same way.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Number of bytes to process after skip. Inf means the whole input.

arguments.name: skip
arguments.text: Bytes to ignore before hashing. "auto" skips the 14-byte binary serialization header.

arguments.name: ascii
arguments.text: Passed to serialize when serialize is TRUE.

arguments.name: raw
arguments.text: If TRUE, return the digest as raw bytes instead of hex.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.text: Seed for xxhash32, xxhash64, murmur32, xxh3_64, and xxh3_128.

arguments.name: errormode
arguments.text: stop aborts. warn warns and returns NA. silent returns NULL.

arguments.name: serializeVersion
arguments.text: Serialization format. 2 is the default.

origin.details: md5, sha1, sha256, and sha512 follow their published specifications. crc32 is the zlib checksum. xxhash32, xxhash64, xxh3_64, and xxh3_128 follow xxHash. murmur32 is MurmurHash3 x86 32. spookyhash is SpookyHash V2 and hashes the serialization itself, skipping with an 8-bit counter. blake3 is BLAKE3. crc32c is the Castagnoli checksum. This package is not meant for cryptographic use.
origin.value: A hex string, or raw bytes when raw is TRUE. Length 32 for md5, 40 for sha1, 8 for crc32, xxhash32, and murmur32, 16 for xxhash64 and xxh3_64, 64 for sha256 and blake3, 128 for sha512, and 32 for spookyhash and xxh3_128.

translation.description: Apply a hash to a Python value that stands in for an R object, or to a file. By default the value is serialized in R's version-2 format and the 14-byte header is skipped.
translation.usage: digest(object, algo="md5", serialize=True, file=False, length=math.inf, skip="auto", ascii=False, raw=False, seed=0, errormode="stop", serializeVersion=None)

arguments.name: object
arguments.text: A str is a length-1 character vector. An int or float is a length-1 double. A bool is logical. None is NULL. bytes is a raw vector. A list is an R list. character(), integer(), real(), data_frame(), and integer_matrix() build the other vectors the example needs.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: Hash algorithm. A unique prefix is accepted. md5 is the default.

arguments.name: serialize
arguments.text: If True, hash the version-2 serialization of the object.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: If True, object is a file path. Passing the path as file= with object omitted is treated the same way.

arguments.name: length
arguments.text: Number of bytes to process after skip. math.inf means the whole input.

arguments.name: skip
arguments.text: Bytes to ignore before hashing. "auto" skips the 14-byte binary header, or through the fourth newline of an ascii serialization.

arguments.name: ascii
arguments.text: If True, serialize as text. Integers are decimal lines, NA is the text NA, reals use %.16g, strings use C escapes, and raw bytes are two hex digits.

arguments.name: raw
arguments.text: If True, return the digest as bytes instead of hex.

arguments.name: seed
arguments.text: Seed for xxhash32, xxhash64, murmur32, xxh3_64, and xxh3_128. A negative seed sign-extends to 64 bits, matching as.integer passed to a uint64 parameter.

arguments.name: errormode
arguments.text: stop raises DigestError. warn warns and returns NA. silent returns None.

arguments.name: serializeVersion
arguments.text: Serialization format. None uses 2.

translation.details: A Python int is an R double, matching the literal 1. integer() builds an R integer, matching 1L. NA is R's missing value and is distinct from a plain NaN. Data-frame matrices are split into columns the way data.frame() does, and automatic row names are stored as c(NA, -n).
translation.value: A hex string, or bytes when raw is True.
translation.example:
from digest import character, data_frame, digest, integer_matrix
print(digest([
    character(list("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ")),
    data_frame(
        a=character(list("abcde")),
        b=integer_matrix(list(range(1, 11)), ncol=2),
    ),
]))
